name: Tindersticks
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Six people from Nottingham named themselves after a box of German matches, demoed their first album in a Kilburn kitchen and spent a decade making strings, soul and Claire Denis scores. Half of them left in 2006; the other half built a studio in a French barn and kept going.

hero.by: Tindersticks in Budapest, May 2012. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A box of matches on a Greek beach
eras.text: Asphalt Ribbons lost their label when Marc Riley's In-Tape Records closed. The same people renamed themselves, moved to London, started their own label and within a year had Melody Maker's album of the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Wikipedia: Asphalt Ribbons · Wikipedia: Stuart A. Staples · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: Asphalt Ribbons become Tindersticks
years.p: Stuart Staples, David Boulter, Neil Fraser, Dickon Hinchliffe, Al Macaulay and Mark Colwill take a new name from a box of German matches Staples found on a Greek beach.
years.xp:
Staples had been singing in Nottingham bands since 1983, first Indignant Desert Birds, then Asphalt Ribbons, whose line-up by 1991 was all but Tindersticks already. Some Asphalt Ribbons songs carried over.

Most of them had known each other since the mid-1980s, from Nottingham clubs, gigs and record shops, bonding over Young Marble Giants, Joy Division and the Velvet Underground, the Guardian's Jude Rogers wrote in 2008. Her piece has Colwill recruited on bass in time for the first album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Patchwork on Tippy Toe, the band's own label
years.p: By now the six had moved from Nottingham to London. The first London gig follows in December at the Islington Powerhaus.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1993 album)
years.h: Jarvis Cocker co-directs the City Sickness video
years.p: Martin Wallace, then working with [[Pulp|76b2e842-5e85-4c97-ab62-d5bc315595b5]], shoots it with [[Jarvis Cocker|38550441-d437-4aff-867e-e79bf0c04142]] in Hyde Park. Boulter pushes a buggy holding Staples' baby daughter Sydonie.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1993 album) · Tape Op · No More Workhorse · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008) · Guardian: Cult heroes: Tindersticks (2016)
years.h: The first album, demoed in a Kilburn kitchen, wins Melody Maker over
years.p: Out on This Way Up, it's Melody Maker's album of the year. [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] and Mark Radcliffe both champion it; Radcliffe names it his favourite of 1993.
years.xp:
Staples told Tape Op the band made its first demos in a kitchen in Kilburn. "It was so exciting recording the first album," he said in 2021, "recording it as a 26-year-old."

Tindersticks played the first night of Radcliffe and [[Marc Riley|9b872fea-1c8e-42f8-878d-c8356de79bba]]'s late-night Radio 1 show on October 25. By March 1994 the album had sold over 20,000 copies in the UK.

It was a double album. "Most of us had jobs, so it was purely about escape," Staples told the Guardian in 2008, "rushing home from work with that hunger to get things done."

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1995 album)
years.h: Blixa Bargeld sends them to a studio in Cologne
years.p: On tour supporting [[Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds|172e1f1a-504d-4488-b053-6344ba63e6d0]], they took Blixa Bargeld's tip and spent a week at Conny's Studios, where most of the second album's backing tracks were cut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1995 album)
years.h: Sleepy Song, recorded on one microphone in one night at Abbey Road
years.p: [[Terry Edwards|4f9f3ee1-e2cf-4d6a-8e5c-9412b42a3bad]] writes the string arrangements, recorded at Abbey Road a few days later. The album is mixed in the house the band shared.

eras.title: Tailored suits and a string section
eras.text: The second album went Top 20, the live shows grew orchestras, and a French director started asking for scores. By Curtains the band could feel its sound running out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
yt: No More Affairs, live at the Bloomsbury Theatre
years.h: A full string section at the Bloomsbury Theatre
years.p: The London show becomes the live album The Bloomsbury Theatre 12.3.95, which reaches No. 32.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1995 album)
years.h: The second Tindersticks, and the band in new suits
years.p: The cover shows Fraser being fitted at Timothy Everest's London atelier. Travelling Light is a duet with Carla Torgerson of The Walkabouts, and the album reaches No. 13.
years.xp: Boulter later said they'd always worn ill-fitting second-hand suits, so the fitting was a treat for their hard work. Drugstore's Isabel Monteiro speaks a monologue on My Sister, and the No More Affairs video was filmed at the Rivoli Ballroom in south-east London.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Wikipedia: Nénette and Boni · Cinema Scope: A Marriage Made in Heaven (2011)
years.h: The first score for Claire Denis: Nénette et Boni
years.p: Seven Denis films would follow with Tindersticks scores, and Staples and Hinchliffe each scored others on their own.
years.xp: It started with Denis asking to use My Sister in the film. By 2011 the run had reached White Material, which Staples and Boulter worked on from a rough assembly while Staples was in France and Boulter in Prague, per Cinema Scope.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: Curtains, and the band's biggest single
years.p: Bathtime reaches No. 38. The album was cut at Eastcote Studios in London, and by now, Staples said later, the band had started worrying about studio time and arrangements.
years.xp: "There was this sense of non-reality about those first two records," Staples told the Guardian in 2008. By Curtains it had become a job: "We stopped making music in a subconscious way."

eras.title: Soul, then Beggars Banquet
eras.text: The band turned toward soul on its last Island album, then moved to Beggars Banquet for two more records and a film score. Musical differences came to a head making Waiting for the Moon.

years.src: Wikipedia: Simple Pleasure · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Simple Pleasure lists how many takes each song took
years.p: Short, direct soul songs with female backing vocals and a cover of Odyssey's If You're Looking for a Way Out. It reaches No. 4 on Greece's international chart and isn't released in the US.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Tiny Tears plays in the first season of The Sopranos
years.p: The song runs through the episode "Isabella". Years later a 14-minute Running Wild mix closes the show's penultimate episode.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: A Four Tops cover is the first Beggars single
years.p: What Is a Man, recorded as the theme for the BBC series The Sins, comes out on Beggars Banquet and reaches No. 90.

years.src: Wikipedia: Can Our Love... · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Can Our Love..., the first album on Beggars
years.p: More soul, a nod to The Chi-Lites in Chilitetime, and a Metacritic score of 81. It reaches No. 47.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trouble Every Day · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Their Trouble Every Day score plays to walkouts at Cannes
years.p: Claire Denis's horror film, with Vincent Gallo and Béatrice Dalle, polarized the festival; Beggars Banquet put out the soundtrack.

years.big: "It has a feeling of something that was lost."
q: It has a feeling of something that was lost.
years.src: Wikipedia: Waiting for the Moon · Wikipedia: The Hungry Saw · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: Waiting for the Moon closes the first era
years.p: David Boulter, who later named it his least favourite Tindersticks album. Musical differences came to a head during the sessions, and the band went on hiatus.
years.xp:
Recorded between September 2001 and January 2003 at Great Linford Manor and home studios, the album includes 4.48 Psychosis, after Sarah Kane's play. Boulter said the band "hadn't been great for a couple of albums."

Staples put it down to fatigue: by 2003 he wanted a simpler set-up, and got it on solo records made in his small house in Lewisham, per the Guardian.

eras.title: Leaving songs
eras.text: Staples moved into solo records and his own label, Hinchliffe into film scores. The six played together one more time, and it convinced half of them to keep going.

years.cap: Stuart Staples, Mod Club Theatre, Toronto
years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Wikipedia: The Hungry Saw · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: Staples starts Lucky Dog and goes solo
years.p: Lucky Dog Recordings 03-04 comes out in 2005 and Leaving Songs, on Beggars Banquet, in 2006. Hinchliffe scores Ira Sachs's Forty Shades of Blue.
years.xp:
Staples' notes on Leaving Songs called them songs "written on the verge of leaving the things I loved," closing a way of writing he had started long before.

During the break Staples and Boulter also made a children's album together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks (1995 album) · Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Wikipedia: The Hungry Saw · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008) · Guardian: Tindersticks, Barbican, London (2006)
years.h: The original six play their second album at the Barbican, then three leave
years.p: For All Tomorrow's Parties' Don't Look Back series, with nine strings and two brass players including [[Terry Edwards|4f9f3ee1-e2cf-4d6a-8e5c-9412b42a3bad]]. Hinchliffe, Colwill and Macaulay leave afterwards.
years.xp:
Staples called the night a happy triumph "tinged with sadness" at knowing the six had made all the new music they would make together. "I had thought it was over," he told the Guardian two years later; the gig made him want to make another album.

Maddy Costa's Guardian review counted roughly six sentences from Staples all night, one of them "We all know what's going to happen next." The strings were joined by trombone, trumpet and a musical saw, and the encores ran to City Sickness and My Sister played twice.

eras.title: A barn in Limousin
eras.text: Staples, Boulter and Fraser built a studio behind Staples' house in France and brought in new players. Staples says it took three albums for the second line-up to really click.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Hungry Saw · Tape Op · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: The band builds Le Chien Chanceux in a 200-year-old barn
years.p: Staples had moved his family to Limousin in 2006, and the barn studio was ready by June 2007. The three originals write and record there with Dan McKinna on bass, Thomas Belhom on drums and Ian Caple engineering.
years.xp: "We plugged in the tape machines, set up the microphones and everything worked like a dream," Staples told the Guardian. Playing without the other three "felt like cheating on someone" for a while, he said, "but at the same time, this was our life's work."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Hungry Saw · Guardian: It was time to look each other in the eye (2008)
years.h: The Hungry Saw, the first new Tindersticks in five years
years.p: Out on Beggars Banquet, it keeps the soul-leaning sound the band had been working since Simple Pleasure. Critics praised its consistency.
years.xp:
The cover is a heart Staples cut into the cream kitchen paintwork of his French house, with a list of song titles. "I did it with a screwdriver," he told the Guardian. "To properly mark our new start."

In the meantime The Sopranos had been introducing the early records to a new audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: Falling Down a Mountain · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Falling Down a Mountain moves to 4AD and Constellation
years.p: Earl Harvin takes the drums and Irish songwriter David Kitt joins on guitar. Uncut heard "a band with restored self-belief."

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Hinchliffe scores Winter's Bone
years.p: Debra Granik's film is Oscar-nominated. He has worked as a full-time film composer since leaving the band, later scoring Locke and a series of Peaky Blinders.

years.src: No More Workhorse · Wikipedia: Tindersticks · The Quietus: Staples' Diet (2012)
years.h: The Something Rain, when the new band clicked
years.p: Staples singles it out: after The Hungry Saw and Falling Down a Mountain, this is when the second line-up came together. They tour it as a five-piece.
years.xp: "Recording Medicine (on The Something Rain) was very exciting," Staples told No More Workhorse. It was the band's ninth album, made at his French studio, and he told the Quietus's Jude Rogers in 2012 that it felt "like this is a second chance." The previous record had been frustrating to make.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · Tape Op
years.h: Across Six Leap Years: old songs re-cut at Abbey Road
years.p: Having let the 20th anniversary pass, the band re-records ten songs from across its catalogue and Staples' solo years, with brass from Julian Siegel.

eras.title: Albums with films attached
eras.text: The band kept making records in France and scoring Claire Denis's films, and gave one album a short film for every song.

years.src: Tape Op · Wikipedia: Lhasa de Sela · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: The Waiting Room finally releases the duet with Lhasa de Sela
years.p: Staples recorded Hey Lucinda with his friend Lhasa in Montreal, then shelved it after her death in 2010. Every song on the album also got a short film, one by Claire Denis.
years.xp: "After that she became ill and we lost her, and I had to put the song away for a long time," Staples told Tape Op. Lhasa died of breast cancer on January 1, 2010. Savages' Jehnny Beth sings on We Are Dreamers!, which Staples heard right after seeing her at a David Lynch tribute night.

years.cap: Odeon of Herodes Atticus, Athens, July 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks · No More Workhorse
years.h: Robert Pattinson sings Willow
years.p: The end-titles song from Denis's High Life, scored by Staples, is credited to Tindersticks featuring Pattinson. No Treasure But Hope follows later in the year.

years.src: No More Workhorse · Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Distractions opens with an 11-minute song
years.p: Made during the pandemic after the 2020 tour was cancelled, it reaches No. 15 in Germany. Staples said it felt like it took five times as long as it should have.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tindersticks
years.h: Soft Tissue, album fourteen
years.p: Thirty-two years after Patchwork, Staples, Boulter and Fraser are still at the core of the band.
